subject: Private staging: throughput & burst targets — kickoff
messages:
From: Alice Drake <alice@orionsys.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Peter Sun <psun@edgeops.io>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 May 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Private staging: throughput & burst targets — kickoff

Hi team,

Thanks for taking this on. We’re preparing to move a subset of Orion’s inference traffic into a private VPC deployment with Redwood for our staging environment across two regions. The main asks for this kickoff:

- Confirm sustained throughput target (qps / tokens/sec) we should size for per-region.
- Define burst headroom and how sustained vs burst policies interact with autoscaling.
- Identify networking constraints (eg. egress limits, private peering) that will affect achieved throughput.
- Agree on a short validation plan (smoke tests + 1x synthetic ramp).

I’ve attached a short QPS profile export (orion_qps_profile.csv) showing observed 30-day percentiles and a sample 5-minute tail spike histogram. We’ll need an ops-oriented plan rather than a pure arch doc — how many GPUs, warm caches, and what fallback behavior.

Proposed participants from our side: Mateo (ops/infra lead), Marissa (customer success), Naomi (performance SME). I’ve looped Peter from EdgeOps (our networking partner) in case we need peering changes.

Can you confirm availability for a 30–45m sync this week?

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Drake
Head of Platform Engineering
Orion Systems

Attachments: orion_qps_profile.csv (CSV, 68KB)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alice Drake <alice@orionsys.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Peter Sun <psun@edgeops.io>
Date: Mon, 13 May 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private staging: throughput & burst targets — kickoff

Alice — thanks for the context and for the profile. I pulled the CSV and gave it a quick pass. High level: the 95th/99th qps windows suggest a mixed traffic pattern with regular spikes ~3–4x sustained baseline for short intervals. That maps well to a "sustained + burst" model but we should avoid sizing purely for peak.

Immediate next steps from Redwood side:
1) Naomi will produce a first-draft sizing estimate (GPU count / effective concurrency / expected token/sec) for the two-region staging footprint.
2) I’ll sketch a validation runbook template (staging-runbook-v1.md) that specifies warm cache flows, synthetic ramp, and the fallbacks (route to hosted, throttle curve).
3) We’ll pull network egress thresholds from Peter and propose a CIDR/peering plan.

For the sync: I’m available Wed 16th 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 17th 08:30–09:15 PT. If either works I’ll send an invite and attach the runbook draft.

Notes on constraints we’ll account for in the draft:
- Cache warmup: when routing cold requests to private pool we expect a 2–5x latency multiplier for initial tokens until KV warmed per model.
- Autoscale window: default 60s evaluation with synthetic warmup may not catch 30s spikes — we’ll recommend short burst buffers and a small reserved headroom.
- Networking: single-AZ peering can cap aggregate throughput; plan for dual-AZ tunnels if sustained > 2.5k qps.

Attaching runbook stub in the follow-up.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Deployment Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alice Drake <alice@orionsys.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Peter Sun <psun@edgeops.io>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private staging: throughput & burst targets — kickoff

On Mon, May 13, 2028 at 11:02 AM Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alice — thanks for the context and for the profile. I pulled the CSV and gave it a quick pass.

Thanks — dug into the numbers and attached a quick sizing spreadsheet (sizing-estimate.xlsx). Highlights from my read:

- Observed baseline: ~650 qps per region (median working set). 95th windows in your CSV push to ~1.8k qps. Short 1–5m spikes hit ~2.4–2.8k.
- Recommended staging target per region: "sustained" = 1,200 qps, with burst headroom to 3,000 qps for 3–10m windows. That gives runway for growth while keeping costs predictable.
- GPU mapping (rough): for the current model family (FP16, KV cache enabled), 1 A100-80GB equiv can sustain ~180–220 qps depending on sequence length. Tentative mapping: 6–8 GPUs active for sustained load, scale out to 14 GPUs for burst buffer.
- Warm cache prefetch: suggest pre-warming 20% of highest-frequency KV prefixes before expected ramp windows to reduce cold token penalty.
- Network egress: at 3,000 qps with 1024-token avg responses, expect ~3.2 Gbps egress per region (account for TLS and header overhead). Confirm peer bandwidth per tunnel.

Accepted risks and mitigations in the sheet: warmup lag, model quantization variance, and cross-AZ egress. I’ve left a couple of cells for Peter to fill (peer bandwidth and any cloud egress policys).

Next steps I recommend for the sync:
- Align on sustained vs burst numbers (target above).
- Confirm peering bandwidth and whether dual tunnels are acceptable.
- Run a smoke test (30m synthetic ramp) on a Friday window when we can monitor and roll back.

-naomi
Naomi Feldman
Performance & Inference Optimization, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sizing-estimate.xlsx (Excel, 52KB)

From: Alice Drake <alice@orionsys.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Thanks Naomi — this is exactly the kind of operational breakdown we need. Wed 16th 10:00 PT won’t work for us anymore but Thu 17th 08:30 PT is perfect. Please send a calendar invite for Thu 17th 08:30–09:00 PT and include the runbook and sizing sheet.

Action items we’ll own before the sync:
- Confirm peering capacity with our network team and share tunnel egress numbers (Peter).
- Provide a list of traffic windows so Redwood can pre-warm KV prefixes ahead of the smoke test.
- Share an internal contact for on-call during the validation run.

If the runbook recommends an intermediate canary (small percentage routed to private), we’ll accept that approach.

Appreciate the practical sizing. See you on Thu.

Best,
Alice
Alice Drake
Head of Platform Engineering, Orion Systems
